rv.q: There's bones of a solid play in 'Shaw vs. Tunney.' Unfortunately, they're without flesh.
Grippo Stage Company's new World Premiere production is a knockout event in two acts.
This is arguably the best work this writer has ever seen from Chicago veteran Richard Henzel as Shaw; so many creative layers of his own presented in a philosophic ball, at once malleable and strong.
I think my next step is to read the book as I am certain there will be additional anecdotes that will be as enjoyable as the ones in this beyond-excellent production.

cn.t: Critics find this world premiere about the unlikely friendship between boxer Gene Tunney and George Bernard Shaw fascinating but uneven, with strong performances elevating a script that sometimes struggles with static pacing.
